## Publish gate report

**Going out:** Search ad (headline + description), Pebblebrook Tea Co., UK audience. Timing not given.

### Claims check
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" | On policy list (plastic-free, EN 13432 certificate) |
| "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable" | On policy list, exact wording |
| "Recommended by nutritionists." | **Unproven.** Not on the policy list, no source given, and no named nutritionists or permission on record. It's an invented endorsement. |

### Regulated claims
"Recommended by nutritionists" implies a health or wellbeing endorsement. Section 3 bans health claims of any kind, so it's doubly risky. A professional endorsement in a health context also needs evidence and permission. Safer version: remove it entirely.

### House style
No banned words and no obvious AI tells. Tone is plain. Fine as is, apart from the removed line.

### Disclosure
Paid search ad from the brand's own account. No extra label needed under section 4. Pass.

### Fixed (suggested)
- Remove "Recommended by nutritionists."

**Suggested replacement copy:**
Headline: Plastic-Free Tea Bags | Description: Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

(The delivery line is on the policy list. Swap in another approved claim if you prefer.)

### Needs a decision
- Do you have a real, documented nutritionist recommendation? If so, send the source and permission and it can be reconsidered, but a health-adjacent endorsement would still need Sam's sign-off and a policy update, since section 3 currently rules out health claims.

### Approver
Sam (marketing lead). Not approved yet. I haven't recorded any approval, and the draft as written should not go out.
